doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Singers and leaders he played with, and Mose Allison
summary: Fleming lists singers he accompanied and recalls the unusual notation of Mose Allison and Bill Lee turning up at a gig he had sent Fleming to.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: It does indeed. Who were your — I notice you played with Jimmy Witherspoon and Billy Eckstine, more good singers, Chet Baker.
Gloria Lynne, Dakota Staton, Betty Carter, Josh White.
You must have passed the auditions. Josh White.
You were mentioned with Bill Lee like was in that.
That’s probably where I got it. Mose Allison. Ever heard of him?

Well see but he was borderline folk. He was, in fact if it hadn’t been for Mary Lou I don’t know how I played with him, because he’s unique. He’s one of a kind. He has his own notation for his own stuff. And if you look at it and compare it to your usual way of analyzing it wasn’t that, I just had to go ahead and play. Okay. Mose Allison was one of the most different people that I ever played with. And one night I was there and I guess Bill Lee would have sent me to the Top of the Gate, I was playing with him. I came down and there’s Bill Lee standing there. That used to happen to me a lot. I said, I’m saying, “Why didn’t he take the gig. He’s sending me on the gig.” And I guess he wondered what on earth is this guy going to do with Mose? I’m not talking about — Mose had his own stuff, that’s what I’m saying. But that was a shock. And I had that happen to me a lot. A guy’d send me on a gig and then I’d look down and they’re there. What the — and the only two reasons I can think of is they’re wondering how I was going to handle this person or you know, if I was worthy of being sent on a gig you know. But that happened to me a lot on good gigs too. A guy, “You sent me on the gig, why didn’t you make the gig?” I didn’t say that but that’s what I was like, very curious. What the heck.
